summary: A triangular steel-and-aluminium tower on Sullivan's Island, lit 15 June 1962 to replace the eroding Morris Island light; the last major lighthouse built in the US.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: modern Coast Guard-staffed light with no keeper roster (USLHS roster for Sullivans Island lists none; no ca-style register exists for 1962-1976). Mike Sejman is named only as LighthouseFriends names him, quoted from a 1976 Charleston Observer piece (paraphrased in the story). Disagreements left in the text: tower height (140 / ~150 / 162.5 / 163 ft; likely different measurements), lantern ladder 25 vs 35 ft, candlepower reduction date (1967 / 'five years' / 'a decade'), automation date (1975 per Wikipedia, 1976 per LighthouseFriends, 1982 per usalights), NPS transfer (2007 per Wikipedia/AP summary, 29 May 2008 per LighthouseFriends). The USCG Historian page and current Light List could not be read (403), so the light's present lit status rests on LighthouseFriends 2008 text and a 2015 magazine; 'Sources differ on whether the light is still lit' not resolved. The NRHP nomination (73001703) is for the Coast Guard Historic District; its lighthouse description is garbled OCR and calls the lighthouse both contributing and (in other texts) non-contributing; the nomination appears to carry 1993 amendment dates. Record says Morris Island first lit 1768 (USLHS), NPS says 1767. Record's structures list a 1876 stone tower and 1960 steel tower as this station's; the 1876 tower is the Morris Island Light (separate record us-sc-morris-island) and likely should not be attached here. Designer: Wikipedia says 'Thomas Sullivan', all other sources say Jack Graham. Wikipedia used for leads only. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Sejman's service span set to 1970-1979 (source says only 'the 1970s'); NPS (1894/1895) and LighthouseFriends (1898) disagree on the life-saving station date and the story now says so.

corrections.why: NPS: the 1876 tower is on Morris Island and was decommissioned when the Sullivan's Island light was built.
